A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ESR study. All main-text and appendix pages are readable, and the corresponding experiments, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original steering, meta-prompting, latent-ablation and fine-tuning experiments, including supplementary controls and activation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds prefix controls, held-out-prompt evaluation, Wikipedia-derived steering and human validation of an exploratory judge.

M1.justification: The core SAE steering, threshold calibration, contrastive latent selection, ablation, meta-prompting and masked LoRA training procedures remain unchanged. The 26 'off-topic detectors' are renamed 'self-correction-associated latents'; the new vector and prefix procedures are evaluation controls.

E1.justification: V2 extends the retained recovery task with 20 disjoint prompts spanning biology, history, economics, physics and literature. It also evaluates Wikipedia-derived perturbations and prefilled response scenarios (Appendices A.3.5–A.3.8), providing targeted additional coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Wikipedia-derived residual-stream vectors as an evaluated comparison with SAE steering, plus clean-prefix and matched steered/no-prefill comparators in Sections 3.6–3.7. The original five-model and matched random-latent comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include discovery-disjoint evaluation, four off-topic prefill lengths, 447 matched-prefix episodes scored by a separate continuation-only judge, and blind human validation of 40 responses. Appendix A.2.2 also corrects the reference judge from Sonnet to Haiku, aligning it with the main text without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of text-conditioned restarts, resistance beyond generic on-topic context, positive- versus negative-effect latent subsets on held-out prompts, and generalization beyond SAE vectors. Appendix A.2.3 additionally analyzes the holistic judge's false positives. The boost sweep, random-latent control and temporal activation analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: The Wikipedia-vector experiment introduces Wilson confidence intervals and a two-proportion test (Appendix A.3.6). Existing confidence-interval reporting and the three independent random-ablation sets are retained; an increase in repeated-run counts is not reported.

E6.justification: Original results, including the 3.8% Llama-3.3-70B ESR rate, remain unchanged. New results include 3.6% ESR with Wikipedia vectors, 7.0–13.5% restart rates under unsteered prefilling, and continuation scores of 8.7, 30.4 and 54.5 in Table 6. Table 4 adds held-out ESR rates of 5.0% without ablation versus 3.3%, 2.9% and 3.8%; its combined-ablation row does not support the blanket 30–45% reduction claim. Human validation also reveals holistic-judge overscoring.

T1.justification: The steering and ablation equations and threshold definition in Appendices A.1.3–A.1.4 are unchanged. The new metrics table consolidates existing definitions and their standard relationship; no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the dedicated consistency-checking-circuit claim with narrower causal involvement of a latent set. Detection versus sustained resistance becomes a central contribution, generalization beyond SAE directions is newly claimed, and the fine-tuning conclusion is explicitly restricted to one training recipe.

C2.justification: V1 interprets ESR and prompting effects as evidence of internal monitoring circuits. V2 allows restarts to be text-conditioned and considers richer corrective context alongside internal mechanisms as explanations for sustained recovery. It adds substantive limitations concerning steering paradigms, implicit-recovery measurement, heterogeneous latent functions and the generality of its fine-tuning findings.

D1.justification: V2 documents the holistic judge's full prompt, Wikipedia-vector construction and prefix preparation, and explicitly states that fine-tuning used no active steering. It discloses that detailed matched-steering counts were not preserved. Existing implementation details, LoRA hyperparameters and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds a focused comparison with reasoning-model 'aha moments', citing Guo, Yang and Zhou and colleagues. New citations to Huang, Gur-Arieh and Ameisen and colleagues support caution about SAE feature descriptions. These additions refine the existing positioning within self-correction and interpretability research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list and discussion are extensively rewritten around detection and sustained resistance. Terminology changes throughout, metric explanations are consolidated, and new Sections 3.6–3.7 move the existing sequential-activation discussion to Section 3.8.

P2.justification: All 21 original figures are retained. V2 adds a matched-prefix bar chart, a judge-versus-human scatterplot, a metrics table and three control-results tables. Existing displays are repositioned and renumbered, with revised captions, while the overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the match between claims and evidence by retreating from v1's dedicated-monitoring-circuit interpretation and directly testing text-conditioning alternatives. Held-out evaluation and disclosure of the failed holistic judge address additional validity concerns. Missing matched-steering counts and Table 4's inconsistent reduction claim remain weaknesses, but the stronger controls and more defensible interpretation provide a substantial overall improvement.
